decisions.reason: As a prominently launched 'new product line' with its own page and clear fit with the firm's core practice software business, management is likely to justify continued commitment and blame any weak uptake on gradual digitization in dental practices rather than abandon it.

The training institute is more peripheral to the software core and was only mentioned rather than heavily showcased, but it still supports customer relationships, so an escalation-of-commitment management would be somewhat reluctant to shut it quickly.

A remote support tool is closely complementary to the installed software base and can be defended as service infrastructure, which makes management more likely to continue it despite only modest public commitment.

The analytics dashboard had its own page and aligns with the strategic move toward data-driven practice management, so prior investment and public positioning make continued support more likely than withdrawal.

A complete dental practice bundle appears central to a broad solution strategy for the firm's core market, and management would be inclined to persist because it has visibly committed to an integrated offering.

The job and practice listing portal looks the most peripheral, platform-like, and only lightly committed product, so if results disappoint management has the weakest basis for continued escalation and is most likely to cut it.
